frame_check.frame: APUG 563 f. 179v and f. 181r (crops on the Wuerzburg page, images botschaft_1a.jpg and botschaft_2.jpg)
frame_check.saw: Not the Gregorian repository viewer (EMLO page never loaded; archimede.imss.fi.it/kircher/563/large/ is 403 and the Stanford Luna Insight route is obsolete). I saw two crops of the cryptogram leaves reproduced by Vollrath (Wuerzburg), captioned Ausschnitte aus APUG 563 179v und 181r. 179v: a circle containing a 12x12 grid of the numbers 1-144 in scrambled order (41 80 11 74 12 90 ...), with a 4-line Latin instruction above in Kirchers hand (in quadrato hoc numeros continens ... ). 181r: a circle with a 12x12 grid of Latin syllables (vo tus sint ri prin quan to lu ...), a Latin note above (Jam hic secreta ex praecedenti tabula ...) and a tally of strokes with the number 35. So the cryptogram is a numbered square plus a syllable square, a key-and-message pair, in Latin. No decipherment written on them.
frame_check.note: Page text says the enigma was Kirchers own, sent to the duke, with the dukes receipt dated 29 Sept 1664 answering a letter of 31 Aug; so the cryptogram leaves ff.179-181 look like Kirchers enigma rather than a dukes cryptogram, and the 1 Jun 1664 letter ff.88r-89v was not viewed. Whole leaves not seen, only crops.

title: Ferdinand and Isabella → De Puebla, Tortosa, 28 Dec 1495, cipher copy in Puebla's Great Roman Numeral code
correspondents: Ferdinand and Isabella → Rodrigo González de Puebla
shelfmark: AGS, Patronato Real, LEG,52, DOC.124
folio_note: PARES description 2207846, 4 images (pp. 1-4, foliation 664-665; old mark T. c. Y. 2). Sample decoded: p. 1 ll. 6-8 and p. 2 ll. 1-6; the rest of the cipher copy not decoded.
status: Identified 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #101; targets/puebla1495/): the cipher copy of the despatch of 28 Dec 1495 whose clear draft Bergenroth abstracted in CSP Spain I no. 113 (no. 114 notices the cipher copy, 'substance exactly the same', with no decipherment); five sending dates on p. 2 match no. 113 and no other item. A sample (p. 1 ll. 6-8) decoded with the extant key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33. Open: the cipher copy beyond the sample, and the groups 883, 1374, 1335, 1813, 852, 868, 1221 and 'xxix' (key images not opened: PARES HTTP 429). No page.
why: Anglo-Spanish diplomacy of 1495 (Perkin Warbeck, the Catherine of Aragon marriage treaty) in a code whose 2400-element key survives.
prior_art: checked 27 Oct 2026: content in print as Bergenroth's abstract of the clear draft (CSP Spain I no. 113, pp. 72-75); no decipherment of the cipher copy printed (no. 114); 1868 Supplement starts in 1498

Spanish. 4 images total (664R-665V); only images 1-2 viewed.
